tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

tools.name: mcp__visualize__show_widget
tools.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

schema.name: mcp__visualize__show_widget
schema.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

tools.name: SubagentHandback
tools.description:
Deliver your final report to the agent that spawned you (your caller). Use it once, for that hand-off only: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}). The call ends your run, so do everything else first and put everything your caller needs in that one report. It is not a messaging channel: do not use it for progress updates or questions.

content.content:
# ERN — Jalon 3 : matériel pour revue unique

**Objet :** validation adversariale du Memory Model (spec 1) après les jalons 1 et 2.
**Contenu :** les trois corpus mis à jour, le contrat du pool de handles, le cadrage de la décision `NoLock`, le registre des obligations inter-spécifications.
**Statut :** matériel de conception, non normatif. Version 2 : corrections de la revue unique de GPT intégrées (contrat du pool, corpus, calendrier, scénarios Weld).

## 0. Règles du jalon 3

1. **Oracle indépendant.** Le verdict attendu d'un cas vient de sa source (clause de MM-02 v0.4, de MM-03.3 v0.3, arbitrage, ou usage déclaré), jamais du comportement des modules. Un cas sans source qui tranche est marqué « à arbitrer ».
2. **Jumeau positif.** Chaque rejet a un jumeau minimal accepté : même séquence sans l'élément fautif. Un rejet qui persiste dans le jumeau est un défaut de construction.
3. **États atteints.** Chaque cas est construit depuis l'état initial par des pas autorisés.
4. **Pas de correction silencieuse.** Un verdict obtenu différent de l'attendu est rapporté avec l'état et le pas en cause.
5. **Classement.** Chaque cas relève de : noyau MM-03 (`N3`), machine MM-02 (`N2`), raffinement (`R`), instance de bibliothèque (`Lib` : arène, pool), ou d'une autre spécification (spec 2, 3, 4, 11). Les cas d'une autre spécification restent des obligations inter-spécifications ; ils ne bloquent pas la clôture du jalon 3.
6. **Couverture.** La colonne « Couvert » indique un témoin déjà produit pendant les jalons 1 et 2, quand il est identifié avec certitude. Le jalon 3 rejoue tous les cas depuis l'état initial, couverts ou non, dans un module de cas séparé.
7. **Cible des corpus.** MM3-H et MM23-H sont encodés au jalon 3 sur les brouillons, sans modifier `MM02`, `MM03` ni `MM23`. MM2-H : ses verdicts sont révisés au jalon 3, mais sa validation exécutable reste une obligation de la reconstruction de référence ; le jalon 3 ne le déclare pas validé.
8. **Écarts connus.** Un cas dont le verdict attendu repose sur une décision non encore appliquée au brouillon (MM23-H15, H16) est encodé avec le verdict obtenu, marqué « écart connu », et inscrit au registre de reconstruction. Il n'est jamais présenté comme réussi.

## 4. Contrat du pool de handles (instance de bibliothèque, comme l'arène)

**Principe.** Un handle est une donnée ; il ne porte aucune autorité. La résolution fournit un accès temporaire de seconde classe. Aucun drapeau d'emprunt par entrée : l'exclusivité d'une résolution `Modify` découle des règles du noyau (I1, O3.2), par la forme de l'arbre de dérivation ci-dessous.

**État de l'entrée de pool** (abstrait, comme l'entrée d'arène ; sa représentation en octets est une obligation de l'implémentation) : `{id, storage, internal, slots}`.
- `id` : identité de pool fraîche à chaque `newPool`, jamais réutilisée pendant l'exécution. Un pool détruit puis recréé, même sur le même stockage, a une autre identité.
- `slots` : chaque entrée est `{place, gen : Nat, live : Bool}` ; `place` est une partie de `storage`.
- La valeur pool est le détenteur de `internal` (même règle que F1). Le stockage peut être local, statique, alloué ou un bloc.

**Handle** : `(id, slot, gen)`, une donnée de taille fixe.

**Emprunt composé.** Une résolution est un emprunt composé : une autorité **compagne** dérivée de `internal` sur **tout le stockage** du pool, au mode de la résolution, détenue par le cadre courant ; puis une autorité d'**entrée** par handle résolu, dérivée **de la compagne** (sous-empreinte), au même mode, détenue par le cadre courant et étiquetée de la génération résolue. Conséquences, toutes par les règles existantes du noyau :
- la compagne ne peut être libérée tant qu'une de ses autorités d'entrée est active (O3.2) ;
- une compagne `Modify` active rend le mode effectif de `internal` absent sur tout le stockage : toute nouvelle résolution, `Modify` ou `Observe`, est rejetée, quels que soient les handles ;
- plusieurs compagnes `Observe` coexistent ; une résolution `Modify` est alors rejetée.

**Opérations**

- **`newPool storage internal`** : préconditions de `newArena` (F1, F2, J1) ; identité fraîche ; toutes les entrées libres, générations à 0.
- **`allocSlot pool dst : ok | fail | reject`** : droit de mise à jour sur la valeur pool (`Modify` exerçable ou `writeShared` sur métadonnées `SharedMutable`) ; `dst` est une feuille non `Init`, ne détenant aucune autorité active, de la taille d'un handle, `Modify` exerçable ; `fail` si aucune entrée libre (état inchangé) ; `ok` : une entrée libre devient vivante, son contenu reste `Uninit`, le handle `(id, slot, gen)` est écrit dans `dst`, qui seule passe à `Init`.
- **`resolve h m : ok | fail | reject`** (`m` = `Observe` ou `Modify`) : droit d'exercice de `internal` au mode `m` par la valeur pool ; les vérifications d'identité et de génération lisent seulement les métadonnées et précèdent toute création d'autorité ; `fail` (état inchangé) si `h.id` n'est pas l'identité du pool, si `h.gen` diffère de la génération de l'entrée, ou si l'entrée est libre ; `ok` : emprunt composé à une entrée. Une compagne déjà active n'est jamais réutilisée : chaque résolution crée la sienne.
- **`resolveMany hs m : ok | fail | reject`** : une compagne, une autorité d'entrée par handle (par `split` de la compagne) ; `fail` si un handle est périmé ou d'un autre pool, ou si deux handles désignent la même entrée ; **atomique** : en cas de `fail`, aucune autorité n'est créée. Coût dynamique explicite : vérification de distinction proportionnelle au lot. C'est la voie des requêtes ECS.
- **`unresolve`** : `release` des autorités d'entrée, puis de la compagne.
- **`freeSlot h : ok | fail | reject`** : droit de mise à jour sur la valeur pool ; `fail` si `h` est périmé ou d'un autre pool ; `reject` si une autorité active dérivée de `internal` couvre l'entrée (donc pendant toute résolution du pool, puisque chaque compagne couvre tout le stockage) ; sinon fin logique du contenu de l'entrée **selon `endUse`** (mêmes préconditions : aucune dépendance utilisable, aucune feuille épinglée ; mêmes effets : feuilles `Uninit`, autorités détenues libérées, dépendances supprimées, stockage possédé logiquement mort, sans désallocation) — `reject` si une précondition d'`endUse` échoue ; une entrée déjà `Uninit` est acceptée ; puis l'entrée devient libre et sa génération est incrémentée.

**Invariant `PoolInv`** (tout pool vivant) : entrées deux à deux disjointes et incluses dans le stockage ; toute autorité active dérivée d'une compagne du pool sur une entrée porte la génération courante de l'entrée, et l'entrée est vivante ; toute compagne active a au plus les autorités d'entrée de sa résolution pour descendants.

**Générations et identités** : `Nat` dans le modèle ; le débordement des générations et l'unicité réelle des identités de pool sont des obligations de l'implémentation, classées bibliothèque et spec 11.

**Théorèmes attendus**
- `pool_resolve_stale_fails`, `pool_resolve_other_pool_fails` ;
- `pool_no_stale_access` : aucune autorité active d'une génération périmée ;
- `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive` : sur tout état atteint, au plus une compagne `Modify` active par pool, et alors aucune compagne `Observe` — quelle que soit la séquence de `resolve`, `resolveMany`, `release`, `store`, `transfer` et `unresolve` qui y mène ;
- `pool_resolveMany_atomic` et `pool_resolveMany_distinct` ;
- `pool_freeSlot_ends_content` : après `freeSlot`, le contenu de l'entrée satisfait les effets d'`endUse` ;
- `pool_inv_preserved`, et intégration à `Reachable` dans un module séparé, noyau inchangé.

**Cas** : H30–H34b, H44, W1.

## 5. Décision `NoLock` — cadrage

**Fait établi (passe 7).** Des états atteints contiennent des autorités détenues que personne ne peut exercer, ce qui bloque un `reset` ou un `free` jusqu'à la mort d'une ressource englobante (H49–H51). Ces états respectent tous les invariants de sûreté ; la charte exclut les interblocages du contrat de sûreté (§4.1). C'est une question d'ergonomie et de progrès, pas de sûreté.

**Options**

1. **Aucune règle** (référence de comparaison). Les blocages sont admis ; les relations persistantes passent par des handles par convention.
2. **Règle locale.** Interdire qu'une opération place une autorité dans un emplacement qu'elle couvre (auto-blocage). O8 l'interdit déjà pour `store` ; le gain à mesurer porte sur `transfer` et `issue`. Ne couvre pas les cycles de longueur ≥ 2 construits par autorité auxiliaire.
3. **`NoLock` global.** Acyclicité de la relation « `b` bloque `a` », auto-blocage défini comme clause séparée, vérifiée à l'arrivée de `transfer`, `issue`, `store`.

**Mesures à produire au jalon 3, pour chaque option :**
- faux rejets sur les cas qui doivent être acceptés : H11, H19, H29b, H35–H37, H44–H47, W1–W3 ;
- blocages résiduels sur H49–H51 ;
- coût d'analyse : la vérification est-elle locale à une fonction, ou exige-t-elle une analyse globale ?

**Critère de choix** : aucune option n'est adoptée si elle rejette un cas qui doit être accepté. Entre options sans faux rejet, la moins coûteuse à analyser l'emporte.

cases h₁ <;> cases h₂ <;> first | rfl | contradiction

theorem Guarded.ok_iff {σ : Type} {Pre : Prop} {eff s' : σ} :
    Guarded Pre eff (.ok s') ↔ Pre ∧ s' = eff :=
  ⟨fun h => by cases h; exact ⟨‹_›, rfl⟩, fun ⟨h, e⟩ => e ▸ .ok h⟩

theorem Guarded.reject_iff {σ : Type} {Pre : Prop} {eff : σ} :
    Guarded Pre eff .reject ↔ ¬ Pre :=
  ⟨fun h => by cases h; assumption, fun h => .reject h⟩

/-! ## O1 `derive` (MM-03.3 §3) -/

/-- Effect of `derive(source, place, mode)` (MM-03.3 §3, O1): a new active authority with
origin `src`, footprint `footprint place`, mode `m`, held by the current frame. -/
def deriveEff (s : S3) (src q : Nat) (m : Mode) : S3 :=
  s.addAuth ⟨m, some src, footprint s.P q, .frame s.top, true⟩

/-- O1.4 (MM-03.3 §3): every existing authority stays compatible with the derived one in the
resulting state. Not a precondition of `derive`: it follows from O1.1 and O1.3 under I1
(`derive_compat_redundant`, A11). -/
def DeriveCompat (s : S3) (src q : Nat) (m : Mode) : Prop :=
  ∀ b ∈ List.range s.A.length, ∀ p ∈ footprint s.P q,
    OptP (effective (deriveEff s src q m) b p) (fun e => Compat e m) True

/-- Preconditions of `derive` (MM-03.3 §3, O1), in order: 1 active origin, exercisable at the
requested mode (B2);
place still usable (MM-03.3.1); 2 requested footprint within the origin's; 3 mode permitted by
the effective authority of the origin on each leaf. O1.4 is removed (A11): it follows from the
others under I1 (`derive_compat_redundant`). O1.5 is not restated: `derive` deactivates
nothing. -/
def DerivePre (s : S3) (src q : Nat) (m : Mode) : Prop :=
  s.Active src ∧ s.ExercisableAt src m ∧ s.Usable q ∧
  (∀ p ∈ footprint s.P q, p ∈ s.afp src) ∧
  (∀ p ∈ footprint s.P q, Allows (effective s src p) m)

instance (s : S3) (src q : Nat) (m : Mode) : Decidable (DerivePre s src q m) := by
  unfold DerivePre; infer_instance

/-- `derive` as a relation (MM-03.3 §3, O1). -/
def DeriveStep (src q : Nat) (m : Mode) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (DerivePre s src q m) (deriveEff s src q m)

/-! ## O2 `split` (MM-03.3 §3) -/

/-- Effect of `split(source, regions)` (MM-03.3 §3, O2): one derived `Modify` authority per
region, held by the current frame; the origin remains a logical authority. -/
def splitEff (s : S3) (src : Nat) (rs : List (List Nat)) : S3 :=
  { s with A := s.A ++ rs.map fun r => ⟨.modify, some src, r, .frame s.top, true⟩ }

/-- Exclusive right already distributed by `src` on leaf `p`: an active descendant of `src` in
mode `Modify` covering `p` (MM-03.3 §3, O2.4). -/
def DistribExcl (s : S3) (src j p : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧ src ∈ s.ancs j ∧ p ∈ y.footprint ∧ y.mode = .modify)
    False

instance (s : S3) (src j p : Nat) : Decidable (DistribExcl s src j p) := by
  unfold DistribExcl; infer_instance

/-- Preconditions of `split` (MM-03.3 §3, O2), in order: 1 the origin is an active authority,
exercisable at `Modify` (B2), with effective `Modify` on every leaf of the regions; 2 regions within the available footprint
(the origin's footprint where its effective authority is present); 3 regions pairwise disjoint,
structurally (no shared leaf) or by `DeclaredDisjoint` (MM-03.3.8); 4 no region covers an
exclusive right already distributed. O2.5 is not restated: `split` changes neither `D` nor
activity. -/
def SplitPre (k : K) (s : S3) (src : Nat) (rs : List (List Nat)) : Prop :=
  s.Active src ∧ s.ExercisableAt src .modify ∧ (∀ r ∈ rs, ∀ p ∈ r, effective s src p = some .modify) ∧
  (∀ r ∈ rs, ∀ p ∈ r, p ∈ s.afp src ∧ effective s src p ≠ none) ∧
  rs.Pairwise (fun r r' => (∀ l ∈ r, l ∉ r') ∨ k.DeclaredDisjoint r r') ∧
  (∀ r ∈ rs, ∀ p ∈ r, ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, ¬ DistribExcl s src j p)

instance (k : K) [∀ r r', Decidable (k.DeclaredDisjoint r r')] (s : S3) (src : Nat)
    (rs : List (List Nat)) : Decidable (SplitPre k s src rs) := by
  unfold SplitPre; infer_instance

/-- `split` as a relation (MM-03.3 §3, O2). -/
def SplitStep (k : K) (src : Nat) (rs : List (List Nat)) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (SplitPre k s src rs) (splitEff s src rs)

/-! ## O3 `release` (MM-03.3 §3, A6) -/

/-- Effect of `release(authority)` (MM-03.3 §3, O3; A6: end of a temporary access): the
authority becomes inactive. F4: an authority held by a place `q` leaves the anchors of `q` in the
same transition. -/
def releaseEff (s : S3) (a : Nat) : S3 := match s.A[a]? with
  | some x => { s with
      A := s.A.set a { x with active := false }
      D := fun q => if x.holder = .place q then (s.D q).filter (· != a) else s.D q }
  | none => s

/-- Right of the current frame on a holder (C4): the holder is the current frame, or a place on
which the current frame has exercisable `Modify` (`HasRight`, B2). -/
def HolderRight (s : S3) : Holder → Prop
  | .frame f => f = s.top
  | .place p => HasRight s .modify p

instance (s : S3) (h : Holder) : Decidable (HolderRight s h) := by
  cases h <;> unfold HolderRight <;> infer_instance

/-- Preconditions of `release` (MM-03.3 §3, O3), in order: 1 active authority; 2 no active
descendant; 3 no usable place has `a` as anchor, except the place that holds `a`, whose anchor
`a` is removed by the release (F4); C4: the authority is derived, an authority
without origin is rejected, and its holder is the current frame or a place on which the current
frame has exercisable `Modify` (`HolderRight`). O3.4 (guarantees of associated abstractions) is
not represented in the kernel. -/
def ReleasePre (s : S3) (a : Nat) : Prop :=
  s.Active a ∧
  (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, a ∈ s.ancs j → ¬ s.Active j) ∧
  (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, s.Usable q → a ∈ s.D q → (s.A[a]?).map (·.holder) = some (.place q)) ∧
  OptP (s.A[a]?) (fun y => y.origin ≠ none ∧ HolderRight s y.holder) False

instance (s : S3) (a : Nat) : Decidable (ReleasePre s a) := by unfold ReleasePre; infer_instance

/-- `release` as a relation (MM-03.3 §3, O3). -/
def ReleaseStep (a : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (ReleasePre s a) (releaseEff s a)

/-! ## O4 `transfer` (MM-03.3 §3, A4, A5) -/

/-! ## Shape of a value (J1) -/

/-- Children of the place `x` (MM-03.3.2), in index order. -/
def kids (P : List Place) (x : Nat) : List Nat :=
  (List.range P.length).filter fun r => decide (parentOf P r = some x)

/-- Position of `r` in a list (its length if absent). -/
def posIn (r : Nat) : List Nat → Nat
  | [] => 0
  | a :: l => if a = r then 0 else posIn r l + 1

/-- The part of `dst` that corresponds to the part `r` of `src` (J1), searched within `n` steps:
`dst` for `src`; for another part, the child, at the same position among the children ordered by

/-- Preconditions of `transfer` (MM-03.3 §3, O4), in order: source usable (MM-03.3.1) and
1 initialised; 2 destination usable, without an `Init` leaf, sharing no leaf with the source (F5:
the footprints of source and destination are disjoint, the clause `¬ overlap`, redundant with
clauses 1 and 2 by `transfer_overlap_redundant`),
and still usable once it owns the source's storage (no ownership cycle); exercisable `Modify`
on the source and on the destination (B2); 4 no active derived
access on the source other than those it holds; 5 anchors of the value valid; 6 non-escape
(MM-03.3.6) towards the destination's frame, for the anchors of the value and of the usable
places it owns, whose frame changes with it (A5), each frame read after the transfer (B7);
7 no leaf of the source pinned, statically
(`Pinned`, MM-03.3.8) or dynamically (A8); B8 on the effective anchor (C1): for every dependent
usable after the transfer, if its effective anchor moves with the value, or if the dependent
itself moves (the destination, or a place the value owns), the frame of the effective anchor is
the dependent's frame or an ancestor of it, both frames read after the transfer
(`EffAnchorOK`); G4: `AnchorOrderHeld` in the arrival state, the whole predicate, for every held
authority; J1: the destination has the shape of the source (`SameShape`). O4.3 holds by
construction. -/
def TransferPre (k : K) (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) : Prop :=
  s.Usable src ∧ (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P src, s.I l = .init) ∧
  s.Usable dst ∧ (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P dst, s.I l ≠ .init) ∧ ¬ overlap s.P src dst ∧
  HasRight s .modify src ∧ HasRight s .modify dst ∧
  (transferEff s src dst).Usable dst ∧
  (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, ¬ ActiveDerivedOutside s src j) ∧
  (∀ x ∈ depsOf s src, s.Active x) ∧
  (∀ x ∈ movedDeps s src,
    NoEscape (transferEff s src dst) x ((transferEff s src dst).pframe dst)) ∧
  (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P src, ¬ k.Pinned l ∧ s.pin l = false) ∧
  (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (transferEff s src dst).Usable q →
    ∀ x ∈ (transferEff s src dst).D q,
      (AnchorMoves s src (s.effAnchor x) ∨ q = dst ∨ OwnedWithin s src q) →
      EffAnchorOK (transferEff s src dst) x ((transferEff s src dst).pframe q)) ∧
  AnchorOrderHeld (transferEff s src dst) ∧ SameShape s.P src dst

instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) :
    Decidable (TransferPre k s src dst) := by
  unfold TransferPre; infer_instance

/-- The preconditions of `transfer` other than the shape of the destination (J1): `TransferPre`
without its last clause (`transferPre_iff`). Used to show that a transfer is rejected by the shape
clause alone. -/
def TransferPreBase (k : K) (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) : Prop :=
  s.Usable src ∧ (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P src, s.I l = .init) ∧
  s.Usable dst ∧ (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P dst, s.I l ≠ .init) ∧ ¬ overlap s.P src dst ∧
  HasRight s .modify src ∧ HasRight s .modify dst ∧
  (transferEff s src dst).Usable dst ∧
  (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, ¬ ActiveDerivedOutside s src j) ∧
  (∀ x ∈ depsOf s src, s.Active x) ∧
  (∀ x ∈ movedDeps s src,
    NoEscape (transferEff s src dst) x ((transferEff s src dst).pframe dst)) ∧
  (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P src, ¬ k.Pinned l ∧ s.pin l = false) ∧
  (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (transferEff s src dst).Usable q →
    ∀ x ∈ (transferEff s src dst).D q,
      (AnchorMoves s src (s.effAnchor x) ∨ q = dst ∨ OwnedWithin s src q) →
      EffAnchorOK (transferEff s src dst) x ((transferEff s src dst).pframe q)) ∧
  AnchorOrderHeld (transferEff s src dst)

instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) :
    Decidable (TransferPreBase k s src dst) := by
  unfold TransferPreBase; infer_instance

theorem transferPre_iff {k : K} {s : S3} {src dst : Nat} :
    TransferPre k s src dst ↔ TransferPreBase k s src dst ∧ SameShape s.P src dst := by
  unfold TransferPre TransferPreBase; simp only [and_assoc]

/-- `transfer` as a relation (MM-03.3 §3, O4). -/
def TransferStep (k : K) (src dst : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (TransferPre k s src dst) (transferEff s src dst)

/-! ## O5 `depend` (MM-03.3 §3) -/

/-- Effect of `depend(result, anchor)` (MM-03.3 §3, O5): the anchor joins the dependencies of
the result place; existing dependencies are kept; propagation to containing values is computed
by `depsOf`. -/
def dependEff (s : S3) (q x : Nat) : S3 :=
  { s with D := fun r => if r = q then s.D q ++ [x] else s.D r }

/-- Preconditions of `depend` (MM-03.3 §3, O5), in order: result place usable (MM-03.3.1);
1 valid anchor; 5 non-escape (MM-03.3.6); B3: exercisable `Modify` on the result; C1: the frame
of the effective anchor is the frame of the result or an ancestor of it (`EffAnchorOK`). O5.2
(real origin of the rights or storage) is not representable: the state does not relate a value
to the origin of its content. O5.3 and O5.4 hold by construction. -/
def DependPre (s : S3) (q x : Nat) : Prop :=
  s.Usable q ∧ s.Active x ∧ NoEscape s x (s.pframe q) ∧ HasRight s .modify q ∧
    EffAnchorOK s x (s.pframe q)

instance (s : S3) (q x : Nat) : Decidable (DependPre s q x) := by
  unfold DependPre; infer_instance

/-- `depend` as a relation (MM-03.3 §3, O5). -/
def DependStep (q x : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (DependPre s q x) (dependEff s q x)

/-! ## F4 `store` -/

/-- Effect of `store a p` (F4; G2), the write of a reference into a value: `a` is now held by the
place `p`; `a` joins the anchors of `p`; the leaf `p`, and it only, becomes `Init` (G2). -/
def storeEff (s : S3) (a p : Nat) : S3 := match s.A[a]? with
  | some y => { s with
      A := s.A.set a { y with holder := .place p }
      D := fun q => if q = p then s.D p ++ [a] else s.D q
      I := fun l => if l = p then .init else s.I l }
  | none => s

/-- Preconditions of `store a p` (F4; G2), in order: `a` active, derived (`a.origin ≠ none`), held
by the current frame; `p` usable; exercisable `Modify` on `p` (B2, `HasRight`); `a` covers no leaf
of `p` nor of its owned storage, transitively (A5, `OwnedIn`); `AnchorOrder` for the added
anchor (C1, `EffAnchorOK`): the frame of the effective anchor of `a` is the frame of `p` or one
of its ancestors. G2: `p` is a leaf, the place of a reference (MM-03.3.2, `isLeaf`); `p` holds no
active authority (overwriting an `Init` leaf without authority is allowed); in the arrival state,
`p` is still exercisable at `Modify` by the current frame (`HasRight`,
`store_keeps_target_reachable`). G4: `AnchorOrderHeld` in the arrival state. No inverse
operation exists (F4). -/
def StorePre (s : S3) (a p : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[a]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧ y.origin ≠ none ∧ y.holder = .frame s.top) False ∧
  s.Usable p ∧ HasRight s .modify p ∧
  (∀ l ∈ s.afp a, l ∉ footprint s.P p ∧
    ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, OwnedIn s.P p q → l ∉ footprint s.P q) ∧
  EffAnchorOK s a (s.pframe p) ∧ isLeaf s.P p ∧
  (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun z => z.active = true → z.holder ≠ .place p)
    True) ∧
  HasRight (storeEff s a p) .modify p ∧ AnchorOrderHeld (storeEff s a p)

instance (s : S3) (a p : Nat) : Decidable (StorePre s a p) := by unfold StorePre; infer_instance

/-- `store` as a relation (F4). -/
def StoreStep (a p : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (StorePre s a p) (storeEff s a p)

/-! ## O6 `enterFrame` (MM-03.3 §4, A5) -/

/-- Owner of the local of index `i` of `ls` (parent, owning local, kind) in the new frame `f`:
the owning local if any, the new frame otherwise (A5). -/
def localOwner (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) (f i : Nat) : Holder :=
  match (ls[i]?).bind (·.2.1) with
  | some o => .place o
  OptP (s'.A[p]?) (fun y => y.mode = .modify →
    OptP y.origin (fun o => ¬ s'.ExercisableAt o .observe ∧ ¬ s'.ExercisableAt o .modify) True) True

instance (s' : S3) (p : Nat) : Decidable (ParamOriginHidden s' p) := by
  unfold ParamOriginHidden; infer_instance

/-- Preconditions of `enterFrame` before G1 and G4 (MM-03.3 §4, O6): the calling frame is active
(non-empty stack); each parameter is an active derived authority (`origin ≠ none`) held by the
caller (A3, read since pass 2 without requiring the caller to be the deriving frame); the parent
and the owner of a local are earlier locals; a part has the owner of its parent. -/
def EnterPreBase (s : S3) (ps : List Nat) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) : Prop :=
  s.F ≠ [] ∧
  (∀ a ∈ ps, OptP (s.A[a]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧ y.holder = .frame s.top ∧
    y.origin ≠ none) False) ∧
  ∀ i ∈ List.range ls.length,
    OptP ((ls[i]?).bind (·.1)) (fun r => s.P.length ≤ r ∧ r < s.P.length + i ∧
      (ls[i]?).bind (·.2.1) = (ls[r - s.P.length]?).bind (·.2.1)) True ∧
    OptP ((ls[i]?).bind (·.2.1)) (fun o => s.P.length ≤ o ∧ o < s.P.length + i) True

instance (s : S3) (ps : List Nat) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) :
    Decidable (EnterPreBase s ps ls) := by
  unfold EnterPreBase; infer_instance

/-- Preconditions of `enterFrame` (MM-03.3 §4, O6): those of `EnterPreBase`; G1: in
`enterEff s ps ls`, the state where the new frame has received its parameters, the direct origin of
every `Modify` parameter is exercisable at no mode (`ParamOriginHidden`); G4: `AnchorOrderHeld` in
the arrival state. -/
def EnterPre (s : S3) (ps : List Nat) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) : Prop :=
  EnterPreBase s ps ls ∧ (∀ p ∈ ps, ParamOriginHidden (enterEff s ps ls) p) ∧
    AnchorOrderHeld (enterEff s ps ls)

instance (s : S3) (ps : List Nat) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) :
    Decidable (EnterPre s ps ls) := by
  unfold EnterPre; infer_instance

/-- `enterFrame` as a relation (MM-03.3 §4, O6; A3). -/
def EnterStep (ps : List Nat) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) (s : S3) :
    Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (EnterPre s ps ls) (enterEff s ps ls)

/-! ## O7 `exitFrame` (MM-03.3 §4, A4, A5, A7) -/

/-- Authority `x` survives the exit to stack `F₀`: active, and held by a holder still live once
the frame is popped, through transitive ownership (A4, A5). A7 speaks of an authority held by
a surviving frame; an authority held by a place is read as held by the frame that ends its
owner chain. -/
def Survives (s : S3) (F₀ : Frames) (x : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[x]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧ HolderLive { s with F := F₀ } y.holder) False

instance (s : S3) (F₀ : Frames) (x : Nat) : Decidable (Survives s F₀ x) := by
  unfold Survives; infer_instance

/-- First surviving authority of a list (A7). -/
def firstSurv (s : S3) (F₀ : Frames) (l : List Nat) : Option Nat :=
  l.find? fun z => decide (Survives s F₀ z)

/-- Authority `a` after the exit (MM-03.3 §4, O7; A7): released unless it survives; a surviving
authority is re-attached to its first surviving strict ancestor along `origin`, which is its
origin when that origin survives. -/
def exitG (s : S3) (F₀ : Frames) (a : Nat) (y : Authority) : Authority :=
  if Survives s F₀ a then
    match y.origin with
    | none => y
    | some _ => { y with origin := firstSurv s F₀ (s.ancs a) }
  else { y with active := false }

/-- Effect of `exitFrame` (MM-03.3 §4, O7; A4; A5; A7): return to the caller; each anchor
replaced by the first surviving authority among itself and its ancestors; authorities that do
not survive released; surviving derived authorities re-attached. -/
def exitEff (s : S3) : S3 :=
  match s.F with
  | _ :: F₀ =>
    { s with
      F := F₀
      D := fun q => (s.D q).map fun x => (firstSurv s F₀ (x :: s.ancs x)).getD x
      A := mapI (exitG s F₀) 0 s.A }
  | [] => s

/-- Preconditions of `exitFrame` (MM-03.3 §4, O7; A7; B4): the exiting frame has a caller; every
anchor of a place still usable after the exit has a surviving authority among itself and its
ancestors along `origin`; every surviving derived authority has a surviving strict ancestor;
B4: no leaf of a place that dies with the frame, transitively owned storage included, is
pinned, dynamically (A8) or statically (`Pinned`, MM-03.3.8); G4: `AnchorOrderHeld` in the arrival
state, after the re-anchoring. Otherwise the exit is rejected. -/
def ExitPre (k : K) (s : S3) : Prop :=
  match s.F with
  | _ :: F₀ => F₀ ≠ [] ∧
      (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, ({ s with F := F₀ } : S3).Usable q →
        ∀ x ∈ s.D q, firstSurv s F₀ (x :: s.ancs x) ≠ none) ∧
      (∀ a ∈ List.range s.A.length, Survives s F₀ a → s.org a ≠ none →
        firstSurv s F₀ (s.ancs a) ≠ none) ∧
      (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, s.Usable q → ¬ ({ s with F := F₀ } : S3).Usable q →
        ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, s.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l) ∧
      AnchorOrderHeld (exitEff s)
  | [] => False

instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (s : S3) : Decidable (ExitPre k s) := by
  unfold ExitPre; split <;> infer_instance

/-- `exitFrame` as a relation (MM-03.3 §4, O7). -/
def ExitStep (k : K) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop := Guarded (ExitPre k s) (exitEff s)

/-! ## Abstract reads and writes (MM-03.3 §5) -/

/-- Ordinary read condition of a leaf by authority `a` (MM-03.3 §5, `canRead3`): an effective
authority permits observation, the leaf is initialised, the needed dependencies are valid. The
type and storage contract is not represented. -/
def CanReadLeaf (s : S3) (a p : Nat) : Prop :=
  effective s a p ≠ none ∧ s.I p = .init ∧ DepsValid s p

instance (s : S3) (a p : Nat) : Decidable (CanReadLeaf s a p) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ ∧ _))

/-- `canRead3` (MM-03.3 §5): ordinary read of leaves `ls` by authority `a`, exercisable at
`Observe` (B2). -/
def canRead3 (s : S3) (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat) : Prop :=
  s.ExercisableAt a .observe ∧ ∀ p ∈ ls, CanReadLeaf s a p

instance (s : S3) (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat) : Decidable (canRead3 s a ls) := by
  unfold canRead3; infer_instance

/-- `read3` as a relation (MM-03.3 §5): a read does not change the state. -/
def Read3Step (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (canRead3 s a ls) s

/-- `canWrite3` (MM-03.3 §5): `a` exercisable at `Modify` (B2); on each leaf, effective
`Modify` of `a` and needed dependencies valid. The clause "no other ordinary authority with an
incompatible effective right" is removed (A11): it follows from the first under I1
(`canWrite3_excl_redundant`). The type and storage condition is not represented. -/
def canWrite3 (s : S3) (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat) : Prop :=
  s.ExercisableAt a .modify ∧ ∀ p ∈ ls, effective s a p = some .modify ∧ DepsValid s p

instance (s : S3) (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat) : Decidable (canWrite3 s a ls) := by
  unfold canWrite3; infer_instance

/-- Effect of a write (MM-03.3 §5): written leaves become `Init`. -/
def write3Eff (s : S3) (ls : List Nat) : S3 := { s with I := fun p => if p ∈ ls then .init else s.I p }

/-- `write3` as a relation (MM-03.3 §5). -/
def Write3Step (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (canWrite3 s a ls) (write3Eff s ls)

/-! ## Lemmas on the effective authority (MM-03.3.5) -/

theorem effOf_cases {m m' : Mode} {ds : List Mode} (h : effOf m ds = some m') :
    (ds = [] ∧ m' = m) ∨ (ds ≠ [] ∧ Mode.modify ∉ ds ∧ m' = .observe) := by

/-! ## Dynamic pinning (A8) -/

/-- Preconditions of `pin p` (A8): `p` usable, exercisable `Modify` on `p` (B2; `Modify` for
`pin`, B10). -/
def PinPre (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Prop := s.Usable p ∧ HasRight s .modify p

instance (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Decidable (PinPre s p) := by unfold PinPre; infer_instance

/-- Effect of `pin p` / `unpin p` (A8): the leaves of `p` become pinned or unpinned. -/
def pinEff (s : S3) (p : Nat) (b : Bool) : S3 :=
  { s with pin := fun l => if l ∈ footprint s.P p then b else s.pin l }

/-- `pin` as a relation (A8). -/
def PinStep (p : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop := Guarded (PinPre s p) (pinEff s p true)

/-- Preconditions of `unpin p` (A8): the external use of every leaf of `p` is done
(`ExternalDone`, MM-03.3.8); B3: the right of `pin`, exercisable `Modify` on `p`. -/
def UnpinPre (k : K) (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Prop :=
  (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P p, k.ExternalDone l) ∧ HasRight s .modify p

instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.ExternalDone] (s : S3) (p : Nat) :
    Decidable (UnpinPre k s p) := by
  unfold UnpinPre; infer_instance

/-- `unpin` as a relation (A8). -/
def UnpinStep (k : K) (p : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (UnpinPre k s p) (pinEff s p false)

/-- Pinning changes neither authorities nor places: `WF3` and `Inv3base` are preserved (A8). -/
theorem pinEff_preserves {s : S3} {p : Nat} {b : Bool} (hwf : WF3 s) (hinv : Inv3base s) :
  OptP (s.A[x]?) (fun y => ¬ heldIn s.P p y.holder ∧ ¬ IsRootOf s p y ∧
    HolderLive (endUseS s p) y.holder) True

instance (s : S3) (p x : Nat) : Decidable (EndUseAnchorOK s p x) := by
  unfold EndUseAnchorOK OptP; split <;> infer_instance

/-- Preconditions of `endUse p` (A6). Usability of the anchored places is read after the end:
a place that dies with `p` has no usable dependent afterwards. In order: `p` usable;
exercisable `Modify` on `p` (A2);
no active derived authority on an ending leaf, or descending from an authority that the end
releases (MM-03.3 §3, O3.2), held elsewhere than in `p` and staying live; no
usable place anchored on an authority held by `p`, on its root, or held by a holder that dies;
C5: no ending leaf pinned, dynamically (A8) or statically (`Pinned`), whatever `ExternalDone`
says: external obligations end only through `unpin`. The ending leaves include those of the
owned places, which die (A6). C8: `p` itself stays usable, its leaves `Uninit`. -/
def EndUsePre (k : K) (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Prop :=
  s.Usable p ∧ HasRight s .modify p ∧
  (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, EndUseAccessOK s p j) ∧
  (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (endUseS s p).Usable q → ∀ x ∈ (endUseS s p).D q,
    EndUseAnchorOK s p x) ∧
  (∀ l ∈ List.range s.P.length, EndingLeaf s p l → s.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l)

instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (s : S3) (p : Nat) :
    Decidable (EndUsePre k s p) := by
  unfold EndUsePre; infer_instance

/-- `endUse` as a relation (A6). -/
def EndUseStep (k : K) (p : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (EndUsePre k s p) (endUseEff s p)

theorem endUseS_releases (s : S3) (p : Nat) : OnlyReleases s (endUseS s p) := by

/-- Preconditions of `free p auth` (A6), in order: `p` deallocable by the allocator contract
(`Deallocable`) and `auth` a compatible deallocation authority (`FreeCompat`, MM-03.3.8); `p` a
usable owned root (a part is not a unit of storage, and `WF3` gives a part the `dead` flag of its
parent); exercisable `Modify` on `p` (B2); no active derived authority on a freed leaf, or
descending from a deactivated authority, held elsewhere and staying live; no usable place
anchored on an authority covering `p`, held within `p`, or whose holder dies; no freed leaf
pinned, statically (`Pinned`) or dynamically, without exception (B6: external obligations end
only through `unpin` under `ExternalDone`). -/
def FreePre (k : K) (s : S3) (p auth : Nat) : Prop :=
  k.Deallocable p ∧ k.FreeCompat p auth ∧ s.Usable p ∧ OwnedRoot s p ∧ HasRight s .modify p ∧
  (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, FreeAccessOK s p j) ∧
  (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (freeS s p).Usable q → ∀ x ∈ (freeS s p).D q,
    FreeAnchorOK s p x) ∧
  (∀ l ∈ List.range s.P.length, FreedLeaf s p l → s.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l)

instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned]
    [DecidablePred k.Deallocable] [∀ p a, Decidable (k.FreeCompat p a)] (s : S3) (p auth : Nat) :
    Decidable (FreePre k s p auth) := by
  unfold FreePre; infer_instance

/-- `free` as a relation (A6). -/
def FreeStep (k : K) (p auth : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (FreePre k s p auth) (freeEff s p)

theorem freeS_get (s : S3) (p j : Nat) : (freeS s p).A[j]? = (s.A[j]?).map fun y =>
    have e1 := congrArg Prod.fst e; have e2 := congrArg Prod.snd e
    simp only at e1 e2; subst e1 e2; exact .ok h1 h2 h3 h4

/-- Preconditions of `arena.reset()` (MM-03.3 §6; A10): metadata right; no active authority
derived from `internal`; no usable place anchored on `internal` or on an authority derived from
it. -/
def ResetPre (k : K) (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (via : Nat) : Prop :=
  MetaRight k s ar via ∧
  (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, ar.internal ∈ s.ancs j → ¬ s.Active j) ∧
  (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, x ≠ ar.internal ∧ ar.internal ∉ s.ancs x)

instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable] (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (via : Nat) :
    Decidable (ResetPre k s ar via) := by
  unfold ResetPre; infer_instance

/-- Effect of `arena.reset()` (MM-03.3 §6; A10; J1): the whole storage becomes available, the past
emissions are forgotten; the initialisation of the arena value is unchanged (J1). -/
def resetEff (s : S3) (ar : Arena) : S3 × Arena :=
  (s, { ar with available := s.afp ar.internal, issued := [] })

/-- `arena.reset` as a relation (MM-03.3 §6; A10). -/
def ResetStep (k : K) (ar : Arena) (via : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 (S3 × Arena) → Prop :=
  Guarded (ResetPre k s ar via) (resetEff s ar)

theorem afp_addAuth_lt {s : S3} {y₀ : Authority} {j : Nat} (h : j < s.A.length) :
    (s.addAuth y₀).afp j = s.afp j := by simp only [S3.afp, addAuth_lt h]
  | ok {ar : Arena} {s' : S3} {ar' : Arena} : s.arenas[i]? = some ar →
      IssueStep k ar via region dst s (.ok s' ar') → IssueAt k i via region dst s (.ok (arenaSet s' i ar'))
  | fail {ar : Arena} {s' : S3} {ar' : Arena} : s.arenas[i]? = some ar →
      IssueStep k ar via region dst s (.fail s' ar') → IssueAt k i via region dst s (.fail s)
  | reject {ar : Arena} : s.arenas[i]? = some ar → IssueStep k ar via region dst s .reject →
      IssueAt k i via region dst s .reject
  | none : s.arenas[i]? = none → IssueAt k i via region dst s .reject

/-- Preconditions of `arena.reset()` on the entry `i` of the state (MM-03.3 §6; A10; D3): the entry
exists and is live (an entry whose `internal` is released cannot be reset), and `ResetPre`. -/
def ResetAtPre (k : K) (s : S3) (i via : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.arenas[i]?) (fun ar => s.Active ar.internal ∧ ResetPre k s ar via) False

instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable] (s : S3) (i via : Nat) :
    Decidable (ResetAtPre k s i via) := by
  unfold ResetAtPre; infer_instance

/-- Effect of `arena.reset()` on the entry `i` (D3): `resetEff`, the new logical state written
back. -/
def resetAtEff (s : S3) (i : Nat) : S3 :=
  match s.arenas[i]? with
  | some ar => arenaSet (resetEff s ar).1 i (resetEff s ar).2
  | none => s

/-- `arena.reset` on the entry `i` of the state as a relation (D3). -/
def ResetAtStep (k : K) (i via : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (ResetAtPre k s i via) (resetAtEff s i)

/-- Determinism of `newArena` (D3; F1). -/
theorem newArena_det {st i : Nat} {s : S3} {o₁ o₂ : Outcome3 S3} (h₁ : NewArenaStep st i s o₁)
    (h₂ : NewArenaStep st i s o₂) : o₁ = o₂ := Guarded.det h₁ h₂

/-- First free entry of a pool (report (f): the material does not say which free entry). -/
def firstFree (pl : Pool) : Option Nat := firstFreeF 0 pl.slots

/-- Static preconditions of `allocSlot pool dst` (material §4): the right to update the pool value;
`dst` a usable leaf, not `Init`, holding no active authority, under exercisable `Modify`. The size
of a handle is not represented: MM-03 has no sizes (report (f)). -/
def AllocSlotStatic (k : K) (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (via dst : Nat) : Prop :=
  PoolRight k s pl via ∧ s.Usable dst ∧ HasRight s .modify dst ∧ isLeaf s.P dst ∧
    s.I dst ≠ .init ∧
    ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun z => z.active = true → z.holder ≠ .place dst)
      True

instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable] (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (via dst : Nat) :
    Decidable (AllocSlotStatic k s pl via dst) := by
  unfold AllocSlotStatic; infer_instance

/-- Effect of `allocSlot` on the entry `i` of the pool `j` (material §4): the entry becomes live,
its content stays as it is, the handle is written into `dst`, which alone becomes `Init`. -/
def allocSlotEff (ps : PS) (j : Nat) (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) (sl : Slot) (dst : Nat) : PS :=
  { setPool ps j (setSlot pl i { sl with live := true }) with s := write3Eff ps.s [dst] }

/-- The handle written by `allocSlot` into its destination (material §4: `(id, slot, gen)`). -/
def slotHandle (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) : Option Handle :=
  (pl.slots[i]?).map fun sl => ⟨pl.id, i, sl.gen⟩

/-- `allocSlot pool dst : ok | fail | reject` as a relation (material §4): `reject` when a static
precondition fails or the pool does not exist; `fail`, state unchanged, when no entry is free;
`ok` otherwise, on the first free entry. -/
inductive AllocSlotStep (k : K) (j via dst : Nat) (ps : PS) : POutcome → Prop where
  | ok {pl : Pool} {i : Nat} {sl : Slot} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl →
      AllocSlotStatic k ps.s pl via dst → firstFree pl = some i → pl.slots[i]? = some sl →
      AllocSlotStep k j via dst ps (.ok (allocSlotEff ps j pl i sl dst))
  | fail {pl : Pool} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → AllocSlotStatic k ps.s pl via dst →
      firstFree pl = none → AllocSlotStep k j via dst ps (.fail ps)
  | reject {pl : Pool} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → ¬ AllocSlotStatic k ps.s pl via dst →
      AllocSlotStep k j via dst ps .reject
  | none : ps.pools[j]? = none → AllocSlotStep k j via dst ps .reject

/-! ## `resolve h m` and `resolveMany hs m` (material §4) -/

/-- The handle designates a live entry of the pool, at its generation (material §4, `resolve`:
`fail` "si `h.id` n'est pas l'identité du pool, si `h.gen` diffère de la génération de l'entrée,
ou si l'entrée est libre"). A slot index outside the pool designates no entry (report (f)). -/
def HandleOK (pl : Pool) (h : Handle) : Prop :=
  h.id = pl.id ∧ OptP (pl.slots[h.slot]?) (fun sl => sl.gen = h.gen ∧ sl.live = true) False

instance (pl : Pool) (h : Handle) : Decidable (HandleOK pl h) := by
  unfold HandleOK; infer_instance

/-- Right of the pool value to exercise `internal` at mode `m` (material §4, `resolve`): the
precondition of `derive` (MM-03.3 §3, O1) of the companion, from `internal`, on the whole storage.
It reads the effective mode of `internal`, so an active `Modify` companion rejects every new
resolution, whatever the handles (material §4, H31a). -/
def ResolveRight (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (m : Mode) : Prop := DerivePre s pl.internal pl.storage m

instance (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (m : Mode) : Decidable (ResolveRight s pl m) := by
  unfold ResolveRight; infer_instance

/-- State after the compound borrow of one entry (material §4): the companion `s.A.length`,
derived from `internal` on the storage, then the entry authority `s.A.length + 1`, derived from the
companion on the place `q` of the entry, both at mode `m`, held by the current frame. -/
def resolveS (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (q : Nat) (m : Mode) : S3 :=
  deriveEff (deriveEff s pl.internal pl.storage m) s.A.length q m

/-- `resolve h m : ok | fail | reject` on the pool `j` as a relation (material §4): `reject` when
the right fails; then `fail`, state unchanged, when the handle is stale, of another pool or names
a free entry; `ok` with the compound borrow, recorded with the resolved generation. The derive of
the entry is a kernel step: its precondition is checked (`noEntry`). -/
inductive ResolveStep (j : Nat) (h : Handle) (m : Mode) (ps : PS) : POutcome → Prop where
  | ok {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight ps.s pl m → HandleOK pl h →
      pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl →
      DerivePre (deriveEff ps.s pl.internal pl.storage m) ps.s.A.length sl.place m →
      ResolveStep j h m ps (.ok { ps with
        s := resolveS ps.s pl sl.place m
        res := ps.res ++ [⟨pl.id, pl.internal, ps.s.A.length, m,
          [(ps.s.A.length + 1, h.slot, h.gen)]⟩] })
  | fail {pl : Pool} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight ps.s pl m → ¬ HandleOK pl h →
      ResolveStep j h m ps (.fail ps)
  | reject {pl : Pool} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → ¬ ResolveRight ps.s pl m →
      ResolveStep j h m ps .reject
  | noEntry {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight ps.s pl m →
      HandleOK pl h → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl →
      ¬ DerivePre (deriveEff ps.s pl.internal pl.storage m) ps.s.A.length sl.place m →
      ResolveStep j h m ps .reject
  | none : ps.pools[j]? = none → ResolveStep j h m ps .reject

/-- The handles of a batch all designate live entries of the pool at their generation, and pairwise
distinct entries (material §4, `resolveMany`: `fail` "si un handle est périmé ou d'un autre pool,
ou si deux handles désignent la même entrée"). -/
def BatchOK (pl : Pool) (hs : List Handle) : Prop :=
  (∀ h ∈ hs, HandleOK pl h) ∧ (hs.map (·.slot)).Nodup

instance (pl : Pool) (hs : List Handle) : Decidable (BatchOK pl hs) := by
  unfold BatchOK; infer_instance

/-- Regions of the entries of a batch: the footprint of each designated entry. -/
def batchRegions (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (hs : List Handle) : List (List Nat) :=
  hs.map fun h => footprint s.P (slotPlace pl h.slot)

/-- State after the compound borrow of a batch (material §4): the companion `s.A.length`, then one
entry authority per handle by `split` of the companion (MM-03.3 §3, O2). -/
def resolveManyS (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (hs : List Handle) (m : Mode) : S3 :=
  splitEff (deriveEff s pl.internal pl.storage m) s.A.length (batchRegions s pl hs)

/-- Entry authorities of a batch with their slot and generation: the `i`-th split authority has the
identity `c + 1 + i` for the companion `c`. -/
def batchEntries (c : Nat) (hs : List Handle) : List (Nat × Nat × Nat) :=
  mapI (fun i h => (i, h.slot, h.gen)) (c + 1) hs

/-- `resolveMany hs m : ok | fail | reject` on the pool `j` as a relation (material §4): `reject`
when the right fails; then `fail`, state unchanged and no authority created (atomicity), when the
batch is not valid; `ok` with the compound borrow when the `split` of the companion is accepted,
`reject` otherwise (`noSplit`). -/
inductive ResolveManyStep (k : K) (j : Nat) (hs : List Handle) (m : Mode) (ps : PS) :
    POutcome → Prop where
  | ok {pl : Pool} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight ps.s pl m → BatchOK pl hs →
      SplitPre k (deriveEff ps.s pl.internal pl.storage m) ps.s.A.length
        (batchRegions ps.s pl hs) →
      ResolveManyStep k j hs m ps (.ok { ps with
        s := resolveManyS ps.s pl hs m
        res := ps.res ++ [⟨pl.id, pl.internal, ps.s.A.length, m,
          batchEntries ps.s.A.length hs⟩] })
  | fail {pl : Pool} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight ps.s pl m → ¬ BatchOK pl hs →
      ResolveManyStep k j hs m ps (.fail ps)
  | reject {pl : Pool} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → ¬ ResolveRight ps.s pl m →
      ResolveManyStep k j hs m ps .reject
  | noSplit {pl : Pool} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight ps.s pl m → BatchOK pl hs →
      ¬ SplitPre k (deriveEff ps.s pl.internal pl.storage m) ps.s.A.length
        (batchRegions ps.s pl hs) →
      ResolveManyStep k j hs m ps .reject
  | none : ps.pools[j]? = none → ResolveManyStep k j hs m ps .reject

/-! ## `unresolve` (material §4) -/

/-- Releases the authorities of a list in order (MM-03.3 §3, O3); `none` as soon as a release is
rejected. -/
def releaseAll : S3 → List Nat → Option S3
  | s, [] => some s
  | s, a :: l => if ReleasePre s a then releaseAll (releaseEff s a) l else none

/-- The resolution whose companion is `c`. -/
def findRes (ps : PS) (c : Nat) : Option Res := ps.res.find? fun r => r.comp == c

/-- `unresolve` of the resolution of companion `c` as a relation (material §4: "`release` des
autorités d'entrée, puis de la compagne"): `ok` when every release is accepted, `reject`
otherwise or when `c` is no companion. -/
inductive UnresolveStep (c : Nat) (ps : PS) : POutcome → Prop where
  | ok {r : Res} {s' : S3} : findRes ps c = some r →
      releaseAll ps.s (r.entries.map (·.1) ++ [r.comp]) = some s' →
      UnresolveStep c ps (.ok { ps with s := s' })
  | reject {r : Res} : findRes ps c = some r →
      releaseAll ps.s (r.entries.map (·.1) ++ [r.comp]) = none → UnresolveStep c ps .reject
  | none : findRes ps c = none → UnresolveStep c ps .reject

/-! ## `freeSlot h` (material §4) -/

/-- The handle is current for the pool (material §4, `freeSlot`: `fail` "si `h` est périmé ou d'un
autre pool"): same identity, an existing entry of the same generation. -/
def HandleCur (pl : Pool) (h : Handle) : Prop :=
  h.id = pl.id ∧ OptP (pl.slots[h.slot]?) (fun sl => sl.gen = h.gen) False

instance (pl : Pool) (h : Handle) : Decidable (HandleCur pl h) := by
  unfold HandleCur; infer_instance

/-- An active authority derived from `internal` covers a leaf of the place `q` of an entry
(material §4, `freeSlot`: `reject` "si une autorité active dérivée de `internal` couvre
l'entrée"). -/
def EntryBorrowed (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (q : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∃ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, s.Active j ∧ pl.internal ∈ s.ancs j ∧
    ∃ l ∈ s.afp j, l ∈ footprint s.P q

instance (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (q : Nat) : Decidable (EntryBorrowed s pl q) := by
  unfold EntryBorrowed; infer_instance

/-- Effect of `freeSlot` on the entry `i` of the pool `j` (material §4): the end of the content of
the entry by `endUse` (MM-03.3 §3, O12), then the entry is free and its generation incremented. -/
def freeSlotEff (ps : PS) (j : Nat) (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) (sl : Slot) : PS :=
  { setPool ps j (setSlot pl i ⟨sl.place, sl.gen + 1, false⟩) with
    s := endUseEff ps.s sl.place }

/-- `freeSlot h : ok | fail | reject` on the pool `j` as a relation (material §4), in order:
`reject` without the right to update the pool value; `fail`, state unchanged, for a stale handle
or one of another pool; `reject` when an active authority derived from `internal` covers the
entry; `reject` when a precondition of `endUse` fails; `ok` otherwise. -/
inductive FreeSlotStep (k : K) (j via : Nat) (h : Handle) (ps : PS) : POutcome → Prop where
  | ok {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → PoolRight k ps.s pl via →
      HandleCur pl h → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl → ¬ EntryBorrowed ps.s pl sl.place →
      EndUsePre k ps.s sl.place →
      FreeSlotStep k j via h ps (.ok (freeSlotEff ps j pl h.slot sl))
  | fail {pl : Pool} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → PoolRight k ps.s pl via → ¬ HandleCur pl h →
      FreeSlotStep k j via h ps (.fail ps)
  | reject {pl : Pool} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → ¬ PoolRight k ps.s pl via →
      FreeSlotStep k j via h ps .reject
  | borrowed {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → PoolRight k ps.s pl via →
      HandleCur pl h → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl → EntryBorrowed ps.s pl sl.place →
      FreeSlotStep k j via h ps .reject
  | endUse {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → PoolRight k ps.s pl via →
      HandleCur pl h → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl → ¬ EntryBorrowed ps.s pl sl.place →
      ¬ EndUsePre k ps.s sl.place → FreeSlotStep k j via h ps .reject
  | none : ps.pools[j]? = none → FreeSlotStep k j via h ps .reject

/-! ## Reachability extended with the pool (material §4, "intégration à `Reachable`") -/

/-- One step of the extended machine: a step of `Reachable` (MM-03.3 §10, `Step`) on the kernel
state, or an `ok` pool operation (material §4). -/
inductive PStep (k : K) : PS → PS → Prop where
inductive Op where
  | derive (src q : Nat) (m : Mode)
  | split (src : Nat) (rs : List (List Nat))
  | release (a : Nat)
  | transfer (src dst : Nat)
  | depend (q x : Nat)
  | enter (ps : List Nat) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat))
  | exit
  | read (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat)
  | write (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat)
  | writeShared (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat)
  | pin (p : Nat)
  | unpin (p : Nat)
  | endUse (p : Nat)
  | free (p auth : Nat)
  | alloc (pr ow : Nat) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat))
  | store (a p : Nat)
  | newArena (st i : Nat)
  | issue (i via : Nat) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat)
  | reset (i via : Nat)
  | newPool (st i : Nat)
  | allocSlot (j via dst : Nat)
  | resolve (j : Nat) (h : Handle) (m : Mode)
  | resolveMany (j : Nat) (hs : List Handle) (m : Mode)
  | unresolve (c : Nat)
  | freeSlot (j via : Nat) (h : Handle)

section Exec
variable (k : K) [∀ r r', Decidable (k.DeclaredDisjoint r r')] [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable]
  [DecidablePred k.Pinned] [DecidablePred k.ExternalDone] [DecidablePred k.Deallocable]
  [∀ p a, Decidable (k.FreeCompat p a)] [∀ p ls s, Decidable (k.Satisfiable p ls s)]

/-- `ok` outcome of a step of `Reachable` (MM-03.3 §3–6), `none` otherwise. -/
def kexec (s : S3) : Op → Option S3
  | .derive src q m => if DerivePre s src q m then some (deriveEff s src q m) else none
  | .split src rs => if SplitPre k s src rs then some (splitEff s src rs) else none
  | .release a => if ReleasePre s a then some (releaseEff s a) else none
  | .transfer src dst => if TransferPre k s src dst then some (transferEff s src dst) else none
  | .depend q x => if DependPre s q x then some (dependEff s q x) else none
  | .enter ps ls => if EnterPre s ps ls then some (enterEff s ps ls) else none
  | .exit => if ExitPre k s then some (exitEff s) else none
  | .read a ls => if canRead3 s a ls then some s else none
  | .write a ls => if canWrite3 s a ls then some (write3Eff s ls) else none
  | .writeShared a ls => if WriteSharedPre k s a ls then some (write3Eff s ls) else none
  | .pin p => if PinPre s p then some (pinEff s p true) else none
  | .unpin p => if UnpinPre k s p then some (pinEff s p false) else none
  | .endUse p => if EndUsePre k s p then some (endUseEff s p) else none
  | .free p auth => if FreePre k s p auth then some (freeEff s p) else none
  | .alloc pr ow ls =>
    if AllocStatic k s pr ow ls ∧ k.Satisfiable pr ls s then some (allocEff s pr ow ls) else none
  | .store a p => if StorePre s a p then some (storeEff s a p) else none
  | .newArena st i => if NewArenaPre s st i then some (newArenaEff s st i) else none
  | .issue i via region dst =>
    match s.arenas[i]? with
    | some ar =>
      if IssueStatic k s ar via region dst ∧ Avail ar region ∧ IssueRight s ar region ∧
          AnchorOrderHeld (issueEff s ar region dst).1 then
        some (arenaSet (issueEff s ar region dst).1 i (issueEff s ar region dst).2)
      else none
    | none => none
  | .reset i via => if ResetAtPre k s i via then some (resetAtEff s i) else none
  | _ => none

/-- `ok` outcome of a step of the extended machine, `none` otherwise. -/
def pexec (ps : PS) : Op → Option PS
  | .newPool st i => if NewPoolPre ps.s st i then some (newPoolEff ps st i) else none
  | .allocSlot j via dst =>
    match ps.pools[j]? with
    | some pl =>
      if AllocSlotStatic k ps.s pl via dst then
        match firstFree pl with
        | some i => (pl.slots[i]?).map fun sl => allocSlotEff ps j pl i sl dst
        | none => none
      else none
    | none => none
  | .resolve j h m =>
    match ps.pools[j]? with
    | some pl =>
      match pl.slots[h.slot]? with
      | some sl =>
        if ResolveRight ps.s pl m ∧ HandleOK pl h ∧
            DerivePre (deriveEff ps.s pl.internal pl.storage m) ps.s.A.length sl.place m then
          some { ps with
            s := resolveS ps.s pl sl.place m
            res := ps.res ++ [⟨pl.id, pl.internal, ps.s.A.length, m,
              [(ps.s.A.length + 1, h.slot, h.gen)]⟩] }
        else none
      | none => none
    | none => none
  | .resolveMany j hs m =>
    match ps.pools[j]? with
    | some pl =>
      if ResolveRight ps.s pl m ∧ BatchOK pl hs ∧
          SplitPre k (deriveEff ps.s pl.internal pl.storage m) ps.s.A.length
            (batchRegions ps.s pl hs) then
        some { ps with
          s := resolveManyS ps.s pl hs m
          res := ps.res ++ [⟨pl.id, pl.internal, ps.s.A.length, m,
            batchEntries ps.s.A.length hs⟩] }
      else none
    | none => none
  | .unresolve c =>
    match findRes ps c with
    | some r => (releaseAll ps.s (r.entries.map (·.1) ++ [r.comp])).map fun s' => { ps with s := s' }
    | none => none
  | .freeSlot j via h =>
    match ps.pools[j]? with
    | some pl =>
      match pl.slots[h.slot]? with
      | some sl =>
        if PoolRight k ps.s pl via ∧ HandleCur pl h ∧ ¬ EntryBorrowed ps.s pl sl.place ∧
            EndUsePre k ps.s sl.place then
          some (freeSlotEff ps j pl h.slot sl)
        else none
      | none => none
    | none => none
  | o => (kexec k ps.s o).map fun s' => { ps with s := s' }

/-- Runs a list of operations; `some` of the final state when every step is `ok`. -/
def prun (ps : PS) : List Op → Option PS
  | [] => some ps
  | o :: os => (pexec k ps o).bind fun ps' => prun ps' os

end Exec

section ExecSound
variable {k : K} [∀ r r', Decidable (k.DeclaredDisjoint r r')] [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable]

import Ern.MM03.Horrors
open Ern.MM03 Ern.HandlePool Ern.MM03.Horrors

def dC (s : S3) (src q : Nat) (m : Mode) : List Bool :=
  [decide (s.Active src), decide (s.ExercisableAt src m), decide (s.Usable q),
   decide (∀ p ∈ footprint s.P q, p ∈ s.afp src),
   decide (∀ p ∈ footprint s.P q, Allows (effective s src p) m)]

def tC (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) : List Bool :=
  [decide (s.Usable src), decide (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P src, s.I l = .init),
   decide (s.Usable dst), decide (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P dst, s.I l ≠ .init), decide (¬ overlap s.P src dst),
   decide (HasRight s .modify src), decide (HasRight s .modify dst),
   decide ((transferEff s src dst).Usable dst),
   decide (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, ¬ ActiveDerivedOutside s src j),
   decide (∀ x ∈ depsOf s src, s.Active x),
   decide (∀ x ∈ movedDeps s src,
    NoEscape (transferEff s src dst) x ((transferEff s src dst).pframe dst)),
   decide (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P src, ¬ k.Pinned l ∧ s.pin l = false),
   decide (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (transferEff s src dst).Usable q →
    ∀ x ∈ (transferEff s src dst).D q,
      (AnchorMoves s src (s.effAnchor x) ∨ q = dst ∨ OwnedWithin s src q) →
      EffAnchorOK (transferEff s src dst) x ((transferEff s src dst).pframe q)),
   decide (AnchorOrderHeld (transferEff s src dst)), decide (SameShape s.P src dst)]

def wC (s : S3) (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat) : List Bool :=
  [decide (s.ExercisableAt a .modify)] ++ ls.map (fun p => decide (effective s a p = some .modify)) ++
   ls.map (fun p => decide (DepsValid s p))

def rlC (s : S3) (a : Nat) : List Bool :=
  [decide (s.Active a),
   decide (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, a ∈ s.ancs j → ¬ s.Active j),
   decide (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, s.Usable q → a ∈ s.D q → (s.A[a]?).map (·.holder) = some (.place q)),
   decide (OptP (s.A[a]?) (fun y => y.origin ≠ none ∧ HolderRight s y.holder) False)]

def euC (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (s : S3) (p : Nat) : List Bool :=
  [decide (s.Usable p), decide (HasRight s .modify p),
   decide (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, EndUseAccessOK s p j),
   decide (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (endUseS s p).Usable q → ∀ x ∈ (endUseS s p).D q,
    EndUseAnchorOK s p x),
   decide (∀ l ∈ List.range s.P.length, EndingLeaf s p l → s.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l)]

def frC (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] [DecidablePred k.Deallocable] [∀ p a, Decidable (k.FreeCompat p a)]
  (s : S3) (p auth : Nat) : List Bool :=
  [decide (k.Deallocable p), decide (k.FreeCompat p auth), decide (s.Usable p), decide (OwnedRoot s p),
   decide (HasRight s .modify p),
   decide (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, FreeAccessOK s p j),
   decide (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (freeS s p).Usable q → ∀ x ∈ (freeS s p).D q,
    FreeAnchorOK s p x),
   decide (∀ l ∈ List.range s.P.length, FreedLeaf s p l → s.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l)]

def rsC (k : K) [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable] (s : S3) (i via : Nat) : List Bool :=
  match s.arenas[i]? with
  | some ar => [decide (s.Active ar.internal), decide (MetaRight k s ar via),

def dC (s : S3) (src q : Nat) (m : Mode) : List Bool :=
  [decide (s.Active src), decide (s.ExercisableAt src m), decide (s.Usable q),
   decide (∀ p ∈ footprint s.P q, p ∈ s.afp src),
   decide (∀ p ∈ footprint s.P q, Allows (effective s src p) m)]

def tC (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) : List Bool :=
  [decide (s.Usable src), decide (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P src, s.I l = .init),
   decide (s.Usable dst), decide (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P dst, s.I l ≠ .init), decide (¬ overlap s.P src dst),
   decide (HasRight s .modify src), decide (HasRight s .modify dst),
   decide ((transferEff s src dst).Usable dst),
   decide (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, ¬ ActiveDerivedOutside s src j),
   decide (∀ x ∈ depsOf s src, s.Active x),
   decide (∀ x ∈ movedDeps s src,
    NoEscape (transferEff s src dst) x ((transferEff s src dst).pframe dst)),
   decide (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P src, ¬ k.Pinned l ∧ s.pin l = false),
   decide (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (transferEff s src dst).Usable q →
    ∀ x ∈ (transferEff s src dst).D q,
      (AnchorMoves s src (s.effAnchor x) ∨ q = dst ∨ OwnedWithin s src q) →
      EffAnchorOK (transferEff s src dst) x ((transferEff s src dst).pframe q)),
   decide (AnchorOrderHeld (transferEff s src dst)), decide (SameShape s.P src dst)]

def wC (s : S3) (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat) : List Bool :=
  [decide (s.ExercisableAt a .modify)] ++ ls.map (fun p => decide (effective s a p = some .modify)) ++
   ls.map (fun p => decide (DepsValid s p))

def rlC (s : S3) (a : Nat) : List Bool :=
  [decide (s.Active a),
   decide (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, a ∈ s.ancs j → ¬ s.Active j),
   decide (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, s.Usable q → a ∈ s.D q → (s.A[a]?).map (·.holder) = some (.place q)),
   decide (OptP (s.A[a]?) (fun y => y.origin ≠ none ∧ HolderRight s y.holder) False)]

def euC (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (s : S3) (p : Nat) : List Bool :=
  [decide (s.Usable p), decide (HasRight s .modify p),
   decide (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, EndUseAccessOK s p j),
   decide (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (endUseS s p).Usable q → ∀ x ∈ (endUseS s p).D q,
    EndUseAnchorOK s p x),
   decide (∀ l ∈ List.range s.P.length, EndingLeaf s p l → s.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l)]

def frC (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] [DecidablePred k.Deallocable] [∀ p a, Decidable (k.FreeCompat p a)]
  (s : S3) (p auth : Nat) : List Bool :=

    FreeAnchorOK s p x),

## (f) Décisions non dictées par le matériel

Pool :
1. L'entrée de pool vit à côté de `S3` (`PS`), comme l'entrée d'arène mais hors du noyau. Les résolutions sont un registre fantôme (`Res`) portant les étiquettes de génération.
2. Les entrées sont les enfants du stockage, dans l'ordre des indices. `newPool storage internal` ne reçoit pas de liste d'entrées.
3. `allocSlot` choisit la première entrée libre.
4. Le « droit d'exercice de `internal` au mode `m` » de `resolve` est la précondition de `derive` de la compagne, mode effectif compris. C'est ce qui donne « quels que soient les handles » (H31a).
5. Un handle dont l'entrée n'existe pas : `fail`.
6. `freeSlot` échoue (`fail`) pour un handle périmé ou d'un autre pool seulement ; une entrée libre de même génération n'est pas un échec.
7. « Couvre l'entrée » (`freeSlot`) : couvre une feuille de l'entrée.
8. `allocSlot` reprend les conditions de destination d'`issue`. La taille d'un handle n'est pas représentée : MM-03 n'a pas de tailles.
9. `unresolve` reçoit la compagne. Il libère les autorités d'entrée dans l'ordre enregistré, puis la compagne, et rejette si une libération l'est (y compris celle d'une entrée déjà libérée).
10. `newPool` reprend `NewArenaPre` à la lettre ; sa clause 4 ne lit que les arènes.
11. `PReach` contient toutes les étapes du noyau, et pas seulement `release`, `store` et `transfer`.
12. Lecture de `PoolInv` :
    - troisième clause : sur les descendants actifs à toute profondeur ;
    - deuxième clause : « porte la génération courante » se lit comme une lignée passant par une autorité d'entrée étiquetée de cette génération.
    Les contre-exemples de (d) valent pour les deux lectures de la deuxième clause, celle de l'entrée vivante comme celle de la génération.

MM3-H :
13. H01 encode deux paramètres dérivés de la racine ; la lecture « Observe dérivé du paramètre Modify » est conservée à part (`H01_reborrow`).
14. Choix de construction :
    - H10 : « fin de A » est le `release` de A dérivée ;
    - H11 : fin des blocs par `endUse` de `v2`, puis de la feuille 6 ;
    - H34 : la copie du handle est la lecture d'une feuille puis l'écriture d'une autre ;
    - H44 : les liens sont écrits par les autorités d'entrée ;
    - H51 : construit avec une autorité auxiliaire, puis sa libération ;
    - H07 et H16 : voir (b) 1 et 2 ;
    - W2 et W3 : voir (b) 3 et 4.

MM23-H :
15. La disposition est calculée sur les emplacements de l'exécution : chaque racine a sa propre allocation, dans l'ordre des indices, et chaque feuille 8 octets dans l'ordre des indices. Chaque pas vérifie `NewLayout` dans `Oblig`. H07 « taille 0 » utilise une racine de taille nulle.

`NoLock` :
16. L'auto-blocage porte sur les feuilles du détenteur, sans son stockage possédé.
17. L'option 2 ne vérifie pas `store`, laissé à O8.3.
18. L'acyclicité est une recherche bornée par le nombre d'autorités, complète sur un graphe fini.
19. L'option 3 vérifie l'état d'arrivée entier.

## (g) Questions pour arbitrage

1. **`PoolInv`** n'est pas un invariant de l'extension ((d)). Deux voies :
   - restreindre l'extension : la compagne n'est pas utilisable par les opérations du noyau. Cela ne suffit pas : le ré-ancrage de `exitFrame` et la dérivation depuis l'entrée violent encore les clauses 2 et 3 (`pool_inv_cex_entry`) ;
   - ou réénoncer les clauses 2 et 3, par exemple sur les seules autorités d'entrée, ce que prouve `pool_no_stale_access`.
2. **`resolveMany Observe`** est toujours rejeté par la construction du matériel (`split` exige `Modify`, O2 ; `resolveMany_observe_rejected`). Est-ce voulu ?
3. **Deux pools sur le même `internal`.** `newPool` ne l'interdit pas (clause 4 de `newArena` lue à la lettre). Un `freeSlot` de l'un termine alors le contenu d'une entrée vivante de l'autre.
4. **Passage par valeur vers l'appelé** ((b) 1). Le noyau ne permet pas à l'appelé de prendre une valeur de l'appelant. Le scénario H16 le suppose. Faut-il le relier aux conventions d'appel de la Spec 3 ?
5. **H01.** Un paramètre `Observe` dérivé du paramètre `Modify` sur le même local est accepté à l'entrée (`H01_reborrow`). G1 ne contraint que l'origine des paramètres `Modify`, et les deux autorités sont apparentées (I1). Le verdict attendu « reject » vaut-il aussi pour ce cas ?
6. **W2.** « La vue de colonne » est-elle l'autorité issue du `split`, ou une vue dérivée de celle-ci ? Avec la seconde lecture, le déplacement reste rejeté après sa libération.
7. **W3.** Les blocs sont-ils émis vers des locaux, auquel cas `reset` reste rejeté après `endUse` de la structure, ou dans la structure ?
8. **H51.** Le blocage va au-delà de l'écriture : `v` ne peut plus être terminé par `endUse`, seule la sortie du cadre le libère. L'option 2 ne le prévient sous aucune lecture de l'auto-blocage (feuilles du détenteur, ou stockage possédé comme en O8.3).
9. **H42.** Le développement en ligne droite est accepté par le noyau ; le traitement de `defer` relève de la Spec 3.
10. **Pool non vivant.** `allocSlot` et `freeSlot` n'exigent pas un pool vivant (`internal` actif), et le matériel est muet. `resolve` l'exige par le droit sur `internal`.
